text:
Samir Patel: quick sync — we need a small API handshake between router and console for burn ownership so console can show accurate per-route/unit burn + cache credits. right now console reconstructs from telemetry and it's brittle.
Maya Chen: +1. what's the smallest, orthogonal surface? don't want router to calculate billing.
Jeff Nguyen: maybe router can attach an opaque owner token to responses: `owner_id` + `owner_kind` (route/app/service). console uses that as the canonical ledger key.
Paul O'Keefe: also need an event when a cache hit generates a credit. router can emit `cache_credit_grant` with owner_token and reason. console will join that with token-level burn.
Lena (Console PM): UX ask — we want a realtime preview for canaries: show expected delta if route switches model/quantization. how soon will credits stream?
Samir Patel: proposal: add optional fields in routing response JSON: `owner_token` (string), `owner_kind` (enum: route|tenant|team). router emits telemetry event `credit.awarded` with {owner_token, model_sku, credit_tokens, sample_rate} when a cache-savings is applied.
Maya Chen: telemetry sampling concerns. can we include `sample_rate` so console can extrapolate? also attach `model_sku` and `seq_len_bucket` to improve quality estimates.
Jeff Nguyen: agree. keep events small. schema draft:
```
{ "event": "credit.awarded", "owner_token": "r:42", "model_sku": "rw-7b-q4", "credit_tokens": 12, "sample_rate": 0.05 }
```
Paul O'Keefe: routing teams: will this require any sync between router and quota/econ? if owner_token is just opaque, billing won't change.
Samir Patel: correct — it's additive telemetry only. we intentionally avoid moving money/charge logic into router.
Lena (Console PM): one more: for rollout UX we need a preview API that can simulate credits at route-level for N requests. maybe the router can expose a `preview_credit_estimate` endpoint that returns average credits per-1000 calls.
Maya Chen: that sounds heavier. alternative: console runs a small sampled probe with realtime route headers and aggregates credits client-side using the `credit.awarded` events.
Jeff Nguyen: ops-bot just registered schema name `credit_v1` in internal registry. ops-bot: schema `credit_v1` created at 2024-08-12T15:22:00Z :robot_face:
ops-bot: Note: downstream consumers must handle duplicate events (idempotency key = owner_token + model_sku + seq) and expect sampling.
Paul O'Keefe: edge case: multi-model chains where a single invocation touches multiple model SKUs. Which owner_token gets the credit?
Samir Patel: we discussed split credits: router will emit multiple `credit.awarded` events, each with the owner_token of the original surface that triggered the KV hit (usually the top-level route). console will sum by owner_token.
Lena (Console PM): action items: (1) console: wire `credit.awarded` consumer + sample extrapolation (2) console: add owner_token column into per-route burn table (3) UX: add canary cost preview panel that uses sampled credits.
Maya Chen: dev tasks: (1) router: include `owner_token` in response header `x-owner-token` opt-in flag `X-Emit-Owner-Token` (2) router: emit `credit.awarded` telemetry event whend KV hit credited (3) docs: schema `credit_v1`
Jeff Nguyen: timeline? can we target alpha next sprint for router emit + console consumer PR?
Samir Patel: yes. aim for alpha in 2 weeks. I'll schedule a short sync. if we hit sampling accuracy issues we'll iterate.
Lena (Console PM): sg. I'll put the UX mock in Figma and tag y'all.
Paul O'Keefe: corner: quotas. if owner_token maps to tenant and token is metered differently, console should display note "billing mapping may differ from provider invoice".
Samir Patel: agreed. we'll add a clear tooltip.
Lena (Console PM): thanks — shipping this will make canary cost decisions much easier :sparkles:
Jeff Nguyen: thanks everyone — PRs incoming.
